claim: Scrovegni Chapel full-price daytime ticket is €15 plus €1 presale fee; reduced €11, youth/student €6, special evening ticket €9; same-day bookings not accepted.
quote: Full Price: €15 + €1 presale fee (adults 18+)... Reduced: €11 + €1 presale fee... Youth/Students: €6 + €1 presale fee... Full Price Evening: €9 + €1 presale fee... it is not possible to make reservations for the same day

claim: Scrovegni Chapel visits last exactly 15 minutes, visitors must reach the air-conditioned waiting room 5 minutes before the slot, and automatic doors open only once on entry and exit to stabilise the interior microclimate.
quote: Scrovegni Chapel visits last 15 minutes... visitors must arrive at the air-conditioned waiting room entrance 5 minutes before the visit time printed on their tickets... automatic doors open only once upon entrance and exit, to enable the stabilisation of the interior microclimate

claim: The Padova Urbs Picta combined card costs €28 for 48 hours or €35 for 72 hours, includes unlimited public transport, and covers all eight UNESCO 14th-century fresco sites with one entry per site.
quote: 48-hour ticket: €28; 72-hour ticket: €35; Provincial resident pass: €25 (valid 6 months). Each ticket permits one entry per site and includes unlimited public transportation access

claim: The eight Urbs Picta UNESCO sites are the Scrovegni Chapel, Church of Saints Philip and James in the Eremitani, Palazzo della Ragione, Baptistery of the Cathedral, Chapel of the Carrarese Palace, Basilica and Convent of Sant'Antonio, Oratory of San Giorgio, and Oratory of San Michele.
quote: The sites include the Scrovegni Chapel; Church of Saints Philip and James in the Eremitani; Palazzo della Ragione; Baptistery of the Cathedral; Chapel of the Carrarese Palace; Basilica and Convent of Sant Antonio, Oratory of San Giorgio and the Oratory of San Michele

claim: Basilica of Saint Anthony requires church-appropriate attire, prohibits all photography, animals, food and drink inside; audioguides and disabled access are available.
quote: clothing that is suitable to a church environment... The use of photographic equipment of any kind is prohibited... Animals of any size are not allowed within the Basilica... No food or beverages permitted inside

claim: Basilica of Saint Anthony is open daily from 06:20 to 19:45 in summer and 06:20 to 19:00 in winter, with entry free of charge.
quote: The basilica is open from 06:20 until 19:45 in summer and from 06:20 until 19:00 in winter

claim: Orto Botanico di Padova full ticket is €10, over-65 €8, youth €6, family (2 adults + up to 3 children) €25; last admission 45 minutes before closing.
quote: Full ticket: €10.00, Over 65: €8.00, Special reduced youth ticket: €6.00, Children (0-5 years): free, Family ticket (2 adults + up to 3 children): €25.00... Last admission is 45 minutes before closing time

claim: Palazzo della Ragione opens Tuesday-Sunday 09:00-19:00 (last entry 30 min before closing), full ticket €8 / reduced €6, and its ground floor is the oldest covered market in Europe at over 800 years old.
quote: open from Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with last entry 30 minutes before closing... full ticket price is €8.00... the ground floor of Palazzo della Ragione houses the oldest covered market in Europe, which has been active for more than 800 years

claim: Prato della Valle is a 90,000 m² elliptical square with 78 statues in two concentric rings around the canal-bordered Isola Memmia, hosting a 160-stall Saturday market and an antiques market every third Sunday.
quote: 90,000-square-meter elliptical square... 78 statues (40 in the exterior ring and 38 statues in the inner ring)... Every Saturday is held a traditional market with over 160 stalls, while the antique market takes place every third Sunday

claim: Caffè Pedrocchi's Piano Nobile housing the Museo del Risorgimento opens Tuesday-Sunday 09:30-12:30 and 15:30-18:00 with a €4 ticket; the café itself runs 08:00 to midnight daily, free to enter.
quote: Museum of the Risorgimento is open from Tuesday to Sunday, from 9.30 to 12.30 and from 15.30 to 18.00... The ticket costs €4.00 and includes access to the Pedrocchi Noble Floor

claim: Prato della Valle was reclaimed from swampland in 1775 under Venetian Provveditore Andrea Memmo to a design by architect Domenico Cerato; its statues honour figures including Galileo, Petrarch, Ariosto and Copernicus.
quote: in 1775, Andrea Memmo, the city's Venetian Superintendent, decided to reclaim and restore this area of Padua... He commissioned Domenico Cerato... Key individuals immortalized in these sculptures include authors Ludovico Ariosto and Francesco Petrarch and scientists Galileo Galilei and Nicolaus Copernicus
